title: Fracture fixation surgery
also: plate and screws for a fracture
what: The surgeon puts the broken bone back in place and holds it with a plate, screws, a rod, or wires. This lets the bone heal straight.
why: When the bone pieces have shifted, or the bone will not heal straight in a cast.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours; the hospital stay depends on the case, usually a few days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you smoke. It slows healing
When you last ate and drank

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: No food or drink before surgery. Your doctor will give you the time. For emergency surgery, eat nothing until you ask.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable loose clothes, a phone charger, and the medicines you take every day.

bring: X-rays and the trauma doctor's reports
steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
The anesthetist gives general anesthesia or numbs the limb
The surgeon lines up the bone pieces
The bone is held with metal and checked on X-ray
The wound is stitched, and a bandage and sometimes a splint are applied
feel: It hurts after surgery. You will get painkillers
Swelling and heaviness in the limb for the first days
after: Weight on the limb is increased gradually, as your doctor decides
Follow-up X-rays after a few weeks
The bone usually heals in 6 weeks to a few months
Physical therapy helps bring back movement
red_flags: Pain and swelling in the calf, or the leg feels hot
Fingers or toes turn blue, cold, or numb
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or pus from the wound
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: Will the metal have to come out?
faq.a: Not always. Sometimes it stays for good. The surgeon decides after the bone heals.

faq.q: Will the metal set off airport scanners?
faq.a: It can. Carry your hospital discharge papers to show.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Eat and drink only until the time your doctor gave you. Bring your X-rays and medicine list.
